---
title: "03 - Extract MGtoolbox probability on the 3D manual tracing"
author: "Xinyi Chen"
output: html_document
---

# Purpose

This file examines the MGtoolbox preprocessed signal along the
three-dimensional manual tracing for p28_330_HET_009. It converts
tracing paths into voxel locations, checks that they fall within
the signal volume, and extracts signal values at those locations.

Two measurements are reported: the signal at each exact traced
voxel and the maximum signal in its surrounding 3 × 3 × 3 neighborhood.
Summary statistics and histograms help assess signal quality and
sensitivity to small coordinate or tracing-width differences.

# Steps

1. Library
   Load xml2 to read the manual-tracing file.

2. File paths
   Specify the project directory, sample name, MGtoolbox signal
   file, and manual-tracing file.

3. Read the MGtoolbox 3D probability volume
   Load the three-dimensional preprocessed signal generated
   in Step01 and print its dimensions.

4. Read the manual tracing
   Read the compressed XML file and extract each tracing path's
   X, Y, and Z coordinates. Report the number of control points
   and their coordinate ranges.

5. Rasterize every 3D tracing segment
   Interpolate between consecutive points within each path,
   round the interpolated positions to voxel coordinates,
   and remove duplicates. Check that all resulting voxels
   lie inside the signal volume.

6. Extract exact-voxel MG probabilities
   Convert zero-based image coordinates to one-based R array
   indices and extract the signal at each exact traced voxel.

7. Extract radius-1 maximum probabilities
   Find the maximum signal within a 3 × 3 × 3 neighborhood
   centered on each traced voxel, including the voxel itself.
   Keep this measurement separate from the exact-voxel value
   to assess sensitivity to small spatial offsets.

8. Print the Step 3 check
   Report the number of traced voxels, the number outside
   the volume, and the mean, median, and maximum of both
   signal measurements.

9. Display the two distributions
   Display separate histograms of the exact-voxel signal
   values and the neighborhood-maximum values.

These tracing-based distributions are diagnostic measurements.
They should not be used to select the active-domain threshold,
because the same tracing is later used for validation.

The setup chunk controls R Markdown output formatting and is
separate from these processing steps.
```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## 1. Library

```{r library}
library(xml2)
```

## 2. File paths

```{r paths}
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

  repeat {
    has_readme <- file.exists(file.path(current, "README.md"))
    has_notebooks <- dir.exists(file.path(current, "notebooks"))
    has_data <- dir.exists(file.path(current, "data"))

    if (has_readme && has_notebooks && has_data) {
      return(current)
    }

    parent <- dirname(current)
    if (identical(parent, current)) {
      stop("Open this file from within the repository containing README.md, notebooks/, and data/.")
    }
    current <- parent
  }
}

project_root <- find_project_root()
sample_name <- "p28_330_HET_009"

probability_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "results", sample_name, "01_mgtoolbox_signal",
  "p28_330_HET_009_mg_probability_3d.rds"
)

trace_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data", sample_name, "manual_tracing",
  "p28_330_HET_009_manual.traces"
)
```

## 3. Read the MGtoolbox 3D probability volume

```{r read-probability}
mg_probability_3d <- readRDS(probability_file)

cat("MG probability dimensions (X, Y, Z):\n")
print(dim(mg_probability_3d))
```

## 4. Read the manual tracing

```{r read-tracing}
trace_xml_text <- paste(
  readLines(gzfile(trace_file), warn = FALSE),
  collapse = "\n"
)

trace_document <- read_xml(trace_xml_text)
trace_path_nodes <- xml_find_all(trace_document, "//path")

trace_paths <- lapply(seq_along(trace_path_nodes), function(path_id) {
  point_nodes <- xml_find_all(trace_path_nodes[[path_id]], ".//point")

  data.frame(
    path_id = path_id,
    point_id = seq_along(point_nodes),
    x = as.numeric(xml_attr(point_nodes, "x")),
    y = as.numeric(xml_attr(point_nodes, "y")),
    z = as.numeric(xml_attr(point_nodes, "z"))
  )
})

trace_points <- do.call(rbind, trace_paths)

cat("Tracing control points:", nrow(trace_points), "\n")
print(rbind(
  minimum = sapply(trace_points[c("x", "y", "z")], min),
  maximum = sapply(trace_points[c("x", "y", "z")], max)
))
```

## 5. Rasterize every 3D tracing segment

The tracing coordinates are image coordinates beginning at zero, whereas R
array indices begin at one. We first rasterize the line segments in image
coordinates and add one only when indexing the R array.

```{r rasterize-tracing}
rasterize_one_path <- function(one_path) {
  if (nrow(one_path) == 1) {
    return(data.frame(
      x = round(one_path$x),
      y = round(one_path$y),
      z = round(one_path$z)
    ))
  }

  segment_voxels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(one_path) - 1), function(i) {
    start_point <- as.numeric(one_path[i, c("x", "y", "z")])
    end_point <- as.numeric(one_path[i + 1, c("x", "y", "z")])

    number_of_steps <- max(abs(end_point - start_point))
    number_of_steps <- max(1L, ceiling(number_of_steps))
    interpolation <- seq(0, 1, length.out = number_of_steps + 1L)

    xyz <- outer(1 - interpolation, start_point) +
      outer(interpolation, end_point)

    data.frame(
      x = round(xyz[, 1]),
      y = round(xyz[, 2]),
      z = round(xyz[, 3])
    )
  })

  unique(do.call(rbind, segment_voxels))
}

trace_voxels <- unique(do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(trace_paths, rasterize_one_path)
))

volume_dimensions <- dim(mg_probability_3d)

inside_volume <-
  trace_voxels$x >= 0 & trace_voxels$x < volume_dimensions[1] &
  trace_voxels$y >= 0 & trace_voxels$y < volume_dimensions[2] &
  trace_voxels$z >= 0 & trace_voxels$z < volume_dimensions[3]

cat("Rasterized unique tracing voxels:", nrow(trace_voxels), "\n")
cat("Voxels inside the MG volume:", sum(inside_volume), "\n")
cat("Voxels outside the MG volume:", sum(!inside_volume), "\n")

if (any(!inside_volume)) {
  stop("Some tracing voxels lie outside the MG probability volume.")
}
```

## 6. Extract exact-voxel MG probabilities

```{r exact-probability}
trace_indices <- cbind(
  trace_voxels$x + 1L,
  trace_voxels$y + 1L,
  trace_voxels$z + 1L
)

trace_voxels$mg_probability_exact <- mg_probability_3d[trace_indices]

summary(trace_voxels$mg_probability_exact)
```

## 7. Extract radius-1 maximum probabilities

This second value tolerates a one-voxel registration or line-width difference.
It is reported alongside the exact value; it does not replace it.

```{r radius-one-probability}
neighbor_offsets <- expand.grid(
  dx = -1:1,
  dy = -1:1,
  dz = -1:1
)

radius_one_max <- function(x, y, z) {
  neighbor_x <- x + neighbor_offsets$dx
  neighbor_y <- y + neighbor_offsets$dy
  neighbor_z <- z + neighbor_offsets$dz

  valid <-
    neighbor_x >= 0 & neighbor_x < volume_dimensions[1] &
    neighbor_y >= 0 & neighbor_y < volume_dimensions[2] &
    neighbor_z >= 0 & neighbor_z < volume_dimensions[3]

  neighbor_indices <- cbind(
    neighbor_x[valid] + 1L,
    neighbor_y[valid] + 1L,
    neighbor_z[valid] + 1L
  )

  max(mg_probability_3d[neighbor_indices], na.rm = TRUE)
}

trace_voxels$mg_probability_radius1 <- mapply(
  radius_one_max,
  trace_voxels$x,
  trace_voxels$y,
  trace_voxels$z
)

summary(trace_voxels$mg_probability_radius1)
```

## 8. Print the Step 3 check

```{r check-summary}
step3_summary <- data.frame(
  sample = sample_name,
  rasterized_trace_voxels = nrow(trace_voxels),
  outside_volume = sum(!inside_volume),
  exact_mean = mean(trace_voxels$mg_probability_exact),
  exact_median = median(trace_voxels$mg_probability_exact),
  exact_maximum = max(trace_voxels$mg_probability_exact),
  radius1_mean = mean(trace_voxels$mg_probability_radius1),
  radius1_median = median(trace_voxels$mg_probability_radius1),
  radius1_maximum = max(trace_voxels$mg_probability_radius1)
)

step3_summary
```

## 9.Optional: Display the two distributions

```{r probability-histograms}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

hist(
  trace_voxels$mg_probability_exact,
  breaks = 50,
  col = "grey35",
  border = NA,
  main = "MG probability at exact trace voxels",
  xlab = "MGtoolbox probability"
)

hist(
  trace_voxels$mg_probability_radius1,
  breaks = 50,
  col = "grey35",
  border = NA,
  main = "MG probability within radius 1",
  xlab = "MGtoolbox probability"
)
```

# Decision before Step 4

This step verifies coordinate indexing and measures MG signal on the manual
tracing. Do not choose the active threshold from these tracing distributions,
because the same tracing will later be used for validation.
